messages.author: pagerduty
messages.content: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: api error-rate 6% (1 sample over threshold) — paged on-call at 03:14 UTC

messages.author: alice
messages.content: ack — looking. error rate is already back to 0.4%. another single-sample blip.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: this is the 4th 3am page this week and every one was a single transient spike that self-resolved. our alert pages on ONE breach at 5%.

messages.author: victor
messages.content: could it be the DB connection blips? we saw one around 03:00.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: checked — DB was healthy, the 5xx were a brief upstream timeout that cleared in <30s. so the DB is a red herring.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: root cause of the pager fatigue: should_page has no sustained-breach requirement — a single window at >=5% pages immediately, so transient spikes wake people up.

messages.author: dave
messages.content: proposal: require multiple consecutive breaches before paging, but keep an immediate path for real emergencies.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: Agreed new paging policy: page only after >=3 CONSECUTIVE breaches at >=5% error rate. Keep a critical fast-path: if error rate >=25%, page on the first breach. Anything below 5% never pages.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: 👍 implementing should_page with that, and I'll write the postmortem in #postmortems with the root cause.
